```{python}
#| label: fig-esd-models
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Equivalent circuit of the standardized ESD test models: the model capacitance $C$ is charged to the test voltage via a high-ohmic resistor; closing the switch discharges it into the DUT through the model resistance $R$. HBM: $C = 100\\,$pF, $R = 1.5\\,$kΩ; MM: $C = 200\\,$pF, $R \\approx 0$; CDM: the capacitance is the device itself against ground."

import schemdraw as sd
import schemdraw.elements as elm

sd.svgconfig.svg2 = False

with sd.Drawing(canvas='svg') as d:
    d.config(unit=2, fontsize=10)

    # DUT box first, so its fill stays behind the wiring
    d += elm.Rect(corner1=(8.5, 0.3), corner2=(10.5, 3)).fill('#f4e8d8')
    d += elm.Label().at((9.5, 1.65)).label('DUT')

    # HV source and charging resistor
    d += elm.SourceV().endpoints((0, 0), (0, 3.7)).label(
        '$V_\\mathrm{ESD}$', loc='top')
    d += elm.Resistor().endpoints((0, 3.7), (3, 3.7)).label(
        '$R_\\mathrm{charge}$ (1 MΩ)')

    # model C
    d += elm.Capacitor().endpoints((3, 3.7), (3, 0)).label('$C$',
                                                           loc='bottom')
    d += elm.Dot().at((3, 3.7))
    d += elm.Dot().at((3, 0))

    # discharge switch and model R, dropping into the DUT from the top
    d += elm.Switch().endpoints((3, 3.7), (5.5, 3.7))
    d += elm.Resistor().endpoints((5.5, 3.7), (8.5, 3.7)).label('$R$')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((8.5, 3.7), (9.5, 3.7))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((9.5, 3.7), (9.5, 3))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((9.5, 0.3), (9.5, 0))

    # ground rail
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0, 0), (9.5, 0))
    d += elm.Ground().at((6, 0))
    d += elm.Dot().at((6, 0))
```
